chunks: As for what al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام say: Khums is only in spoils specifically.

So this report may be understood in one of two ways. The first of them is that the intended meaning in it is that khums is only in spoils specifically by the outward wording of the Qur'an, because whatever is besides spoils, the obligation of khums in it was only known through the sunnah (prophetic tradition), and it was not intended that there is no khums in that at all.

And the second way is that these earnings and benefits that accrue to a person are among the spoils that Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in the Qur'an; and he عليه السلام clarified that in the narration that we mentioned at the beginning of the chapter.

key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition) through which further legal obligation is known
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth levy legally due on certain forms of wealth
key_terms.الْغَنَائِمِ: spoils or gains, understood here as the basis for discussing khums
key_terms.الْفَوَائِدُ: benefits or gains received by a person
key_terms.بِظَاهِرِ الْقُرْآنِ: by the apparent wording of the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the obligation of khums on earnings and benefits beyond war spoils?
ai.summary: This report discusses how the ruling of khums is to be understood in relation to "spoils" mentioned in the Qur'an. It explains either that the Qur'an explicitly mentions spoils while the sunnah (prophetic tradition) establishes khums in other cases, or that gains and profits are themselves included within the broader meaning of spoils.
